checkOutcomes.method: Rendered DOM/CSS and targeted CDP probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark emulation produced an identical light consent surface and no preference rule was found.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered DOM/CSS and targeted CDP probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Two infinite 2 s animations remained running while reduce matched.
Lighthouse directly identified insufficient color contrast.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered DOM/CSS and targeted CDP probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: CSS snapshot contains no View Transition declarations across section/article navigation.
CSS snapshot showed no scroll-event animation pattern and no scroll-driven visual effect requiring main-thread linkage; trace had only three bounded long tasks.
CSS probe found native scroll-snap usage and no evidence of custom pointer-driven gesture handling in the rendered entry DOM.

checkOutcomes.method: Navigation DOM and page screenshot review
checkOutcomes.evidence: The portal uses conventional labelled section navigation; no shrinking/progress chrome is necessary to understand the covered pages.
No tooltip, popover or edge-positioned menu was present in the covered initial states.
checkOutcomes.reason: No anchored transient overlay exists in the exercised states.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Descriptive link labels and explicit page headings preserve orientation across homepage, section and article templates.
A full-screen consent gate obscures each public content template.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered DOM/CSS and targeted CDP probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: One full-viewport fixed overlay was present, with zero dialog/popover/details primitives.
The first viewport allocates essentially all visible area to consent chrome instead of requested content.
At 360 px, layout measured 972 px content width and 612 px overflow.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered DOM/CSS and targeted CDP probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: No @container rules were exposed and the consent component fails when reused at mobile width.

checkOutcomes.method: Focus computed style and screenshot review
checkOutcomes.evidence: Programmatic focus on the first action produced a visible 1 px auto outline; primary login controls are large and labelled.
Titles and H1s clearly identify WP, News and the article; link text exposes primary content destinations.
Every public content journey is stopped by the same asymmetric consent decision.
Unknown-route state is hidden by the consent wall and shows no visible recovery.
Lighthouse LCP was 5.2 s; trace LCP was 2.94 s with 78.61 ms TBT.
Layout observer and Lighthouse both measured CLS 0.
Trace recorded three long tasks, 96.12 ms longest and 78.61 ms total blocking time, a bounded main-thread load.
HAR recorded 95 requests, 1.33 MB transfer, 673 KB scripts and 169 KB fonts.
Script delivery dominates the pre-content load at 673 KB across 13 script requests.
Lighthouse failed button-name, link-name and image-alt; image audit found 33 missing alt values.
Lighthouse color-contrast audit failed.
Only one landmark was found and heading order jumps H1 to H3; Lighthouse found an ill-formed accessibility tree.
Desktop consent and login screenshots show readable sizing, line spacing and unclipped text; the failure is reflow, tracked separately.
Lighthouse failed user scaling and mobile layout has 612 px overflow.
Lighthouse best-practices category scored 1.0 and did not report runtime console errors.
Doctype/UTF-8 are valid, but 11 images lack dimensions and 66 are oversized.
Lighthouse reported three BFCache failure reasons.
Homepage and article expose descriptive title and meta description in raw and rendered HTML.
Real href links and indexable robots are present, but Lighthouse failed viewport user scaling and mobile reflow is broken.
Homepage and article return 200, expose canonical links, and homepage robots is index,follow; content survives raw fetch.
Article has social metadata but no JSON-LD structured data block.
HTTPS/CSP/nosniff exist, but HSTS is absent and three observed cookies are not Secure.
Seven third-party origins, DoubleClick and several 390 to 400 day identifiers were observed.
No permission prompt appeared, but the covered account flow offers password sign-in with no WebAuthn/passkey path.
HSTS and Permissions-Policy are absent; referrer policy is no-referrer-when-downgrade.
Article raw HTML retains 67% word coverage but omits its semantic H1.
The fixed consent runtime layer overflows by 612 px on mobile.
This public editorial MPA exposes a manifest/service-worker capability, but its core task is current online news rather than an installable offline app.
checkOutcomes.reason: Offline/installability is contextual and not required for this current-news portal.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The unknown route does not visibly communicate failure or recovery before consent.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM language and CSS logical-property probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTML lang is pl and rendered CSS includes logical inline/block properties.
The Polish news listing renders localized relative timestamps such as “6 min” and “19:48” under lang=pl.
Covered portal pages display publication recency but do not expose a user flow coordinating scheduled events across time zones.
checkOutcomes.reason: No cross-zone scheduling or partial-time user flow exists in the covered scope.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Reject is visually secondary and labelled as a detour to learn more while accept is the direct primary action.
Login fields are not natively required and invalid submission produced no visible field-level recovery before the challenge.
Password has current-password but the login/email field has an empty autocomplete token.
Covered account page clearly exposes password recovery, new-account action, social alternatives and security FAQ; no pricing/continuity commitment is present.
Image audit found 66 oversized images and 11 missing responsive srcset.
Trace found three bounded long tasks and 78.61 ms total blocking time rather than continuous background main-thread work.
Scripts transfer 673 KB and seven third-party origins load before content access.

checkOutcomes.method: Capability probe and contextual applicability judgement
checkOutcomes.evidence: No developer intent or public transaction/tool surface indicates WebMCP capability is expected for this editorial portal.
checkOutcomes.reason: Agent-facing tools are emerging and no agent transaction surface is declared.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The covered editorial and account journeys do not require on-device summarization or generation to complete their core task.
checkOutcomes.reason: On-device inference is an optional enhancement, not necessary for the covered core task.

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline and post-interaction heap summary comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: Ten repeated scroll cycles increased summarized heap self-size only 29,464 bytes (0.09%) and node count by 690 across isolated equivalent loads.
Baseline summarized heap self-size was 32.0 MB for a media-rich portal entry state, proportionate to the page purpose.
Neither heap summary listed Detached constructors among top populations, and repeated-scroll growth was negligible.

principleOutcomes.reason: Agent-facing tools are emerging and no agent transaction surface is declared.

paths.description: Portal homepage and consent entry state, representing the primary discovery journey.
News section listing, representing a major content index template.
Current news article, representing the editorial detail template and crawler visibility.
WP account sign-in, representing the primary account form and authentication journey.
Unknown route, representing HTTP/navigation recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The entry experience does not visibly adapt to dark preference.
findings.evidence: The light and dark screenshots are byte-identical at 108,096 bytes, and the computed CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule while the consent surface stayed white.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply color-scheme: light dark and preference-driven surface/text tokens, including the consent layer.

findings.summary: Animations continue under reduced-motion preference.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe confirmed the media query matched while two running animations, each 2000 ms with unbounded iterations, remained active.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or substantially reduce non-essential repeating animations inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Major cross-document navigation has no View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The authored CSS collected by the DOM probe contained no view-transition usage across a portal dominated by article and section navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin article and section navigation with cross-document View Transitions and a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures all primary content on every public template.
findings.evidence: Desktop homepage, listing and article screenshots show a full-viewport consent wall before content can be used.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface where legally possible, with equal access to accept, reject and manage options.

findings.summary: The blocking consent layer is not exposed as a native dialog.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found one full-viewport fixed overlay but zero dialog, popover or details primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Represent modal consent with a correctly labelled dialog, focus containment and predictable dismissal/choice controls.

findings.summary: The consent experience is unusable at a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout reported scrollWidth 972 versus clientWidth 360, 612 px horizontal overflow; the mobile screenshot starts mid-copy and clips controls off both sides.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove desktop minimum widths from the consent layer, constrain it to 100dvi, and reflow actions and copy intrinsically.

findings.summary: The component-heavy portal exposes no container-query adaptation.
findings.evidence: The rendered stylesheet probe found no @container rules while the same consent component overflows severely on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Use size container queries for reused cards, navigation and the consent component, with intrinsic fallback layout.

findings.summary: The primary content journey is gated by a coercive consent decision.
findings.evidence: All three public archetypes open behind the same full-screen gate, and the reject action is labelled as a detour to learn more rather than an equal direct choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Make reject as immediate and prominent as accept, preserve the requested destination, and avoid requiring a settings detour.

findings.summary: Unknown-route recovery is hidden behind the same consent wall.
findings.evidence: The deliberate unknown URL screenshot shows the consent gate rather than a clear 404 explanation, useful links or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow the error template to communicate status and recovery, then layer consent without hiding that state.

findings.summary: Cold-load LCP is slow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.2 s, Speed Index 6.4 s and time to interactive 8.8 s; the CDP trace separately measured LCP 2.94 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, reduce early consent/advertising work and defer non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: The entry load carries a large early network payload.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 95 requests and 1,334,692 transferred bytes, including 672,657 script bytes and 168,718 font bytes before the user reaches content.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, reduce font variants and tighten cache/dependency chains around the LCP path.

findings.summary: Controls and media lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name, link-name and image-alt; the image audit found 33 images missing alt and the DOM probe found six unnamed buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every interactive control a programmatic name and provide meaningful alt text or explicit empty alt for decoration.

findings.summary: Some foreground/background combinations fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed its color-contrast audit on the rendered entry state.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust text and control color tokens to meet WCAG AA in every preference and consent state.

findings.summary: The homepage structure is sparse and heading order skips levels.
findings.evidence: The probe found only one landmark and a sequence from H1 directly to numerous H3 headings before H2; Lighthouse also reported an ill-formed accessibility tree for agentic browsing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add clear main/nav landmarks and maintain a logical heading hierarchy without skipped levels.

findings.summary: The rendered experience fails Lighthouse user-scaling/reflow checks.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because a rendered viewport context prevents adequate scaling; independent 360 px evidence also shows 612 px overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep user scaling enabled in every document/frame and ensure content reflows at narrow and zoomed widths.

findings.summary: Many images are unsized, oversized or eagerly loaded below the fold.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 11 missing dimensions, 66 oversized images and 77 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions, generate responsive srcset candidates and lazy-load non-critical below-fold imagery.

findings.summary: The page is not eligible for back/forward cache restoration.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove avoidable unload handlers and other BFCache blockers identified in the Lighthouse details.

findings.summary: Editorial pages omit machine-readable structured data.
findings.evidence: The representative article has accurate title/social metadata but its rendered DOM contains zero application/ld+json blocks.
findings.suggestedFix: Add Article or NewsArticle JSON-LD that matches the visible headline, author, dates and primary image.

findings.summary: Transport and cookie defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and CSP are present, but HSTS is absent; three cookies are not Secure and all 16 observed cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable HSTS, mark every HTTPS cookie Secure and narrow SameSite to Lax or Strict unless cross-site use is necessary.

findings.summary: Tracking requests and long-lived identifiers are present on the pre-choice entry load.
findings.evidence: The tracker capture found seven third-party origins including DoubleClick; cookies include multiple identifiers with 390 to 400 day expiry.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay non-essential tracking until valid choice, shorten identifier lifetimes and reduce third-party collection.

findings.summary: Sign-in offers passwords and social providers but no passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login probe found a password field and no PublicKeyCredential/WebAuthn integration.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside recovery-safe fallback methods.

findings.summary: Defensive response policy is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers include CSP, nosniff and X-Frame-Options, but omit HSTS and Permissions-Policy and use no-referrer-when-downgrade.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and adopt strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer handling.

findings.summary: The raw article response omits its semantic H1 and a material share of rendered words.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 67% content overlap for the article and reported h1PresentInRaw false, although the rendered page has one H1.
findings.suggestedFix: Render the full article headline and core semantic content server-side, then enhance it with JavaScript.

findings.summary: The consent runtime state is clipped rather than robust near narrow viewport edges.
findings.evidence: At 360 px the fixed layer remains 972 px wide and controls are partly unreachable.
findings.suggestedFix: Use intrinsic sizing and viewport-safe positioning so overlays never exceed the visual viewport.

findings.summary: The tested unknown route does not expose actionable recovery in the initial state.
findings.evidence: The unknown-route screenshot is indistinguishable from the homepage consent gate, with no visible error status, home link or retry guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Render a useful 404 state before optional layers, including navigation back to current sections.

findings.summary: Consent choices use asymmetric, nudging labels.
findings.evidence: Accept is a strong filled action while reject says “reject and learn more”, implying extra work and withholding a direct equal refusal.
findings.suggestedFix: Use equally clear accept and reject actions, with settings as a separate neutral option.

findings.summary: The login form does not expose native requirements and an attempted invalid submission gives no visible field-level recovery before the challenge.
findings.evidence: The probe found required=false on login/password; the invalid attempt screenshot remained at the challenge with no field-specific error.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare required fields, validate after interaction and announce clear field-level errors before anti-bot verification.

findings.summary: The email/login field omits an autocomplete token.
findings.evidence: The password correctly uses current-password, but the login input autocomplete value is empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Add autocomplete=username to the login field while retaining current-password on the password field.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes through oversized and non-responsive assets.
findings.evidence: The image audit identified 66 images with natural dimensions over twice their displayed size and 11 without srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive modern image candidates sized to their rendered slots.

findings.summary: Third-party and script cost is high before content access.
findings.evidence: The HAR transferred 672,657 script bytes while tracker evidence found seven third-party origins on the consent-gated entry load.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer advertising and analytics until needed and set a third-party byte/request budget.
